title: Beside the Gospel Pool
description: Beside the Gospel Pool in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 112, “The pool of Bethesda. Jn 5:2-4”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-side the gos-pel pool Ap-point-ed for the poor; From year to year, my help-less soul Has wait-ed for a cure.

lines: From year to year, my helpless soul
And others, round me, stepping in
As full of guilt, and fear, and pain.
As when at first I came.
He knows how long I've languished here;
Surely the mercy I have sought
Is not for such as I.
Where streams of sovereign virtue flow
Here then, from day to day,
I'll wait, and hope, and try;
Can Jesus hear a sinner pray,
No: he is full of grace;
A soul, that fain would see his face,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
